newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian opposition begins new rally after clashes.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian opposition begins new rally after clashes.

text.p: Bulgarian opposition supporters began a fresh rally on Saturday outside Sofia's gold-domed cathedral, after riot police put an end to their 10-hour siege of parliament.

State news agency BTA said 97 people were injured in clashes between protesters and police who fired blank cartridges and used clubs to beat a path from the parliament building for trapped deputies from the governing Socialist party early on Saturday.
About 500 to 600 people later gathered around the cathedral and the nearby parliament building, which remained surrounded by riot police and troops.
Ivan Kostov, leader of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces which walked out of the besieged parliament on Friday, called for a nationwide strike and a campaign of civil disobedience.
"It is obvious that there can be no consensus in this parliament and that is why we are leaving," he told the rally.
President Zhelyu Zhelev said he would not ask the ruling Socialist party to form a new government later in the day as expected, because of the protests.
He was to meet his advisory National Security Council on Saturday morning to discuss his next move.

Anger at the country's severe economic crisis spilled over on Friday into the worst political violence since the overthrow of one-party rule in 1989. It came after the Socialists decided to form a new government, ignoring opposition calls for a general election.
BTA said the injured comprised 85 civilians, including two parliamentary deputies from the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces, four security guards from parliament and eight police.
